objective: Declare the three CAN ACK/STOP transport faults as first-class runtime faults, each bound to the CanDiagnosticCode the shipped adapter already emits, so the fault coverage matches the boundary the platform tests.
decision_supported: Whether bus faults belong in the runtime-fault taxonomy rather than in scenario manifests, and whether coverage of them can be claimed without a hardware-tested reference.
acceptance: ack_timeout, stop_timeout and stop_rejected are declared RuntimeFault members with a FaultSpec each
each spec names the CanDiagnosticCode the adapter emits, and a test asserts that name exists
none of the three is added to P2_FAULT_TYPES, because a bus fault is not a scenario property
coverage reports them as SIMULATED, never HARDWARE_TESTED, without a hardware evidence reference
evidence: validate_scenarios.py still reports 12 frozen and 24 expanded manifests
stop_conditions: inducing a fault would need a kernel module, a physical interface or privilege
a fault cannot be asserted against an exact CanDiagnosticCode
the change would alter can_driver_safe.py wire behaviour
risks_and_fallbacks: Adding members to RuntimeFault is additive, but any consumer that iterates it will now see three more values.
Fallback if a fault turns out not to be reachable from the shipped adapter: demote its spec and record it as NOT_EXECUTED rather than deleting it.
No replayable scenario manifest is added yet; the coverage status stays SIMULATED and the README says so.
